Hi Erin — thanks for the list. I’m Marissa on Redwood’s security team; happy to confirm details. Below is a concise Q&A and the operational assurances we can provide for Dedicated deployments. I’ve attached a simplified dataflow diagram and our operational playbook excerpt for region pinning.

Q1 — Region pinning and replication
- Dedicated pools may be provisioned with a region pin (we support AWS us-west-2, us-east-1, and eu-west-1 for Dedicated). When you choose us-west-2, the serving runtime, primary data stores, and snapshots remain in that region.
- We do not perform cross-region replication for customer inference artifacts or token logs by default. Replication only occurs if a customer explicitly requests cross-region failover (documented change request).

Q2 — Isolation and tenancy
- Each Dedicated deployment runs on isolated Kubernetes/GPU node pools logically dedicated to the customer. Network isolation is enforced via VPC peering or PrivateLink (customer choice) with security groups and routing to prevent unintended egress.
- Storage volumes and object stores are provisioned per-customer; metadata indices that assist routing are encrypted at rest and scoped to the deployment ID.

Q3 — Key management and encryption
- At-rest: all persistent volumes and S3 buckets are encrypted. Customers may elect to use Redwood-managed KMS keys or supply a customer-managed key (CMK) in their AWS account (recommended for compliance).
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ between components; internal mTLS between runtime processes.

Q4 — Deletion timelines and mechanics
- API-level deletes: when an API delete call is received for stored artifacts (e.g., training uploads, customer-provided files, evaluation datasets), Redwood marks objects for immediate deletion and triggers a deletion job. For objects in S3/primary stores, deletion completes within 24 hours in normal cases.
- Backups/snapshots: ephemeral snapshots of model serving state (for crash recovery) are retained up to 7 days by default for Dedicated; we can shorten this upon request (e.g., 24–72 hours) and document in the annex. Snapshot deletion is automated and typically completes within 48 hours of retention expiry.
- KV/prefix caches: in-memory KV caches are flushed on pod termination; persistent KV stores follow API delete semantics and are purged within the API delete SLA window (24 hours).
- Long-term archival: Redwood does not archive customer inference payloads into cold storage by default. If an archival policy is enabled for billing or analytics, it will be declared in the contract and you may request opt-out.

Q5 — Proof & auditability
- We provide deletion attestations (timestamped job IDs) for API deletes and snapshot purges.
- Audit logs (access, admin actions) are retained to meet your retention requirement and can be exported to your SIEM via our log-forwarding integration (CloudWatch/Datadog).

Attachment notes:
- redwood-dedicated-dataflow-diagram.svg (shows ingress -> region-bound serving runtime -> KMS location -> logs path)
- region-pin-operational-playbook.pdf (excerpt with operational steps to add/remove region pin, rollback, and deletion verification)

Suggested contract wording (short paragraph for your annex):
"Redwood will provision the Customer's Dedicated deployment in AWS us-west-2 and will not replicate Customer inference data outside that region except upon an explicit, documented request from the Customer for cross-region failover. Redwood will delete Customer data upon request per the deletion SLA: primary-store deletions completed within 24 hours; snapshot purges completed within 48 hours of retention expiry. Redwood will provide a timestamped deletion attestation and relevant audit logs on request."

If that paragraph aligns with what you need, we can produce a signed attestation and include it as an annex. If Seaforth requires shorter snapshot retention or different backup rules, tell us the target and we’ll confirm feasibility.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Security Manager, Redwood Inference

Hi Erin — quick technical confirmation from infra side, and an attestation template attached.

- Snapshots: by default snapshots remain in the provisioning region (us-west-2) and are not automatically copied cross-region. Cross-region replication is only enabled by explicit configuration (change request) and requires an owner-signed approval.
- Attestation fields we emit: request_id, resource_ids (list of object keys), requestor_identity (email), deletion_job_id, deletion_requested_at (ISO8601), deletion_completed_at (ISO8601), operator_id (internal userid), retention_policy_applied (name), region. We provide the attestation as a signed JSON document and can also produce a PDF on request.

Attached: rdw-deletion-attestation-template.json (JSON template stub) — we can pre-populate once you provide a sample object key list or a request_id.

Next step: Prio to contract close, if you want a signed attestation for a few sample deletes we can run one in your Dedicated staging pool and provide the signed output for review. Let me know preferred time windows (we typically schedule these during business hours in us-west-2).

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
